meta.title: Strip Poker Planner — integrated decision dashboard
meta.trip_window: Nov 17 – Dec 23, 2026 (the dates still open on the official Venetian DeepStack Extravaganza IV calendar)
data_pipeline: data/schedule-snapshot.json — every printed row of the official Venetian schedule PDF, re-parsed each morning by tools/sync_official_sources.py
data/structure-audit.json — every structure sheet the calendar links (37 Venetian sheets + Wynn daily/WPT PDFs), field-matched from the fetched PDF text
data/url-checks.json — last-checked date, HTTP status and content hash of each of the 64 tracked official URLs
data/hotel-facts.json — verbatim sentences about resort fee, room tax, parking and cancellation from the official property pages
data/change-log.json — append-only record of official values that moved between runs
meta.verification_policy: A value appears only when it was read on an official operator page or PDF. Anything not printed there is left blank and flagged. Omission of re-entry/add-on wording is never treated as confirmation of single-entry play.
meta.ranking_policy: Rows are ranked only when the total entry fee, the amount reaching the prize pool and the guarantee are all confirmed from the operator's own structure sheet. The guaranteed-pool ÷ entry-fee figure is descriptive arithmetic about the published numbers, not a forecast, expected value or win rate. Bounty, satellite, seniors, ladies, mixed-game and multi-flight rows are listed separately because their payout shape or entry structure changes the comparison.
meta.no_manual_input: Every table, filter and calculation on this site is filled from the data files; nothing here requires you to type anything to read the findings. The trip calculator is pre-loaded with a worked example and only changes if you choose to adjust it.

venues.name: Caesars Palace Poker Room
venues.official_address: 3570 S Las Vegas Blvd, Las Vegas, NV 89109
venues.coverage: No structure sheet is published. The venue's own 2026 daily flyer PDF prints four daily NLH slots — 10 AM $100, 2 PM $160, 6 PM $100, 9 PM $160 — each with 20,000 chips, 20-minute levels and a $1,000 guarantee, plus the fee splits ($70/$30 and $115/$45), the $50 add-on split ($45/$5), registration closing at the start of level 7, and a re-entry rule (re-enter within the first break after elimination). The explore page's blanket 'every event carries a $100 buy-in' sentence conflicts with the flyer's $160 slots — flag F25 records the conflict and the rows follow the dedicated, dated flyer. Rows stay excluded from ranking because the slate prints no calendar dates.

questions.question: Which of these events actually forbid a second entry?
questions.why_it_matters: The whole brief is 'single entry only'. A $300 buy-in becomes $600, $900 or more if re-entries are unlimited, and the guarantee-to-cost comparison changes completely.
questions.we_have: All 37 official structure sheets for the series, read cover to cover on 2026-11-17: each one prints buy-in, house-fee split, guarantee, chips, level length and the late-registration deadline — and no clause about entries, re-entries, rebuys or add-ons. Two sheets (Valuetown bounty events 18/58) instead say 'All subsequent buy in's after the initial buy in will be $200', which positively indicates more than one entry is possible.
questions.missing: A written answer from the Venetian Poker Room (or a rule update on the sheet) stating whether the one-day events are one-entry freezeouts.
questions.how_to_close: Ask the room directly (the poker page lists the contact) and keep the reply as a dated source; until then these rows are labelled 'single-entry unverified' and the toggle filter returns nothing.
questions.owner: you (one e-mail/call) — no agent can produce it

questions.question: What are the exact trip dates, nights and occupancy, and what is the nightly budget and quality floor?
questions.why_it_matters: Hotel rates, cancellation deadlines and 'quality vs cost' are all date- and occupancy-dependent; without them there is no like-for-like comparison and no true nightly cost.
questions.we_have: Mandatory fees that do not depend on dates: $55 + tax resort fee at the Venetian/Palazzo, 13.38% room tax, $20 self-parking / $40 valet per day; $55 + tax at Wynn; $49.95 + tax at Treasure Island.
questions.missing: A dated checkout total (nightly average, fee lines, tax lines) for each candidate hotel on your dates, plus your acceptable nightly ceiling and minimum quality tier.
questions.how_to_close: Price the same dates and occupancy in each official booking flow and paste the itemised totals into the rate log, or authorise a dated-quote step in a follow-up session; until then the calculator uses the advertised starting endpoints and labels them as such.

questions.question: Can a day really start at 8 AM here?
questions.why_it_matters: The brief asks for an all-day schedule beginning at 8 AM.
questions.we_have: Every printed start time on the official calendar: the earliest recurring morning start in the series is 10:10 AM (RaceDay Stack events 3–5, the $1,100 flights and the seniors events); one 9:10 AM turbo satellite exists on Dec 12.
questions.missing: Any official 8:00 AM tournament start on the Strip in this window. None was found on any page checked, so an 8 AM start is not achievable from verified listings.
questions.how_to_close: Either relax the start-time requirement to 'first official flight' (10:10 AM at the Venetian) or name a property whose room opens earlier and have its schedule captured.

questions.question: When does each event actually end?
questions.why_it_matters: 'Primary event + conditional fallback' only works if the earlier event can be finished or exited before the next registration deadline.
questions.we_have: Start time, the printed 'REG CLOSES' deadline for 80 of 93 rows, level count/length and the multi-flight Day-2 restart times from the official schedule and sheets.
questions.missing: Announced finish times — the operator publishes none. Structures with 28 levels at 30 minutes plus six 15-minute breaks describe a 15-hour worst case, so a 5:10 PM entry after an 11:10 AM event is only realistic if you bust out before its own registration closes.
questions.how_to_close: Decide the exit rule (e.g. 'evening event only if bust-out before 4:30 PM') and the schedule page will flag each pair automatically; the underlying math is already wired.

questions.question: How long is the walk from each hotel to each poker room?
questions.why_it_matters: The 30-minute walking rule is a hard filter in the brief; it also decides whether an 8:00 AM-ish start and a late bust-out are survivable.
questions.we_have: Official property addresses and the official statement of where each poker room sits inside its resort (e.g. Venetian poker room on Palazzo level 2, reached from either tower lobby).
questions.missing: Door-to-door walking minutes for every hotel↔venue pair. No property publishes them, and this build environment has no Maps access, so the table is blank by policy, not by oversight.

questions.question: Which guarantee figures are still safe to compare?
questions.why_it_matters: A guarantee that includes bounties, or one shared across several starting flights, is not the same object as a single-flight cash guarantee.

questions.question: What happens to the hotel rate if the poker-rate qualification is missed?
questions.why_it_matters: The headline poker rate is conditional; the true nightly cost can jump to the prevailing rate mid-stay.
questions.we_have: The official qualification terms: six hours of live cash per night, or a $300+ buy-in per night, completed before 2 AM on the last night; otherwise the nightly rate adjusts to the prevailing rate.
questions.missing: The prevailing rate for your dates — which is the number the fallback actually uses.
questions.how_to_close: Get the dated prevailing rate alongside the poker rate in the same booking session and record both in the rate log; note that the $200 events on the calendar do not qualify for the poker rate at all.

questions.question: Which rows moved from 'last verified' to current, and which official pages had to be repointed?
questions.why_it_matters: A row that is current-but-wrong is worse than a row that is stale: it looks checked. Two of this site's unreachable URLs turned out to hide live official successors that changed published values, so the gap is not cosmetic.
questions.we_have: Re-read on 2026-11-17 and updated: Caesars Palace's four daily rows (the 2026 flyer prices 2 PM and 9 PM at $160, not $100, and prints the fee split plus a first-break re-entry) and the Bellagio and ARIA hotel rows (the properties' own reservation terms confirm a $55.00 + tax resort fee, $50 + tax per extra occupant, a 72-hour cancellation deadline, and $20 registered-guest self-parking / $40 valet from the operator rate table). Bellagio's event rows are still unverified on price and re-entry count.

Wynn's $150 Monday-Thursday turbo's structure URL 404s, so its add-on is unpublished and no structure sheet was re-audited against it. ARIA's own $50,000 November deepstack sheet is not in the 2026-11-14 audit.

What still needs a human is the room's answer on the price and entry-rule conflicts, which Q10 and S10 turn into a standing two-document diff.

questions.question: Does any Strip room actually forbid a second entry in writing, and will they put it in an e-mail?
questions.why_it_matters: It is the difference between the brief's single-entry list being empty and being populated. The published sheets for the Venetian series, the Wynn series and the Bellagio weekend events all permit re-entries; the Wynn daily Friday event is the only one that forbids re-entry while still selling unlimited rebuys and an add-on.
questions.we_have: Document evidence only, now including the documents that changed published values today: Bellagio's sheet says players 'buy-in and re-enter through the end of level 8'; Wynn prints 'unlimited re-entry' on 67 of 69 event sheets and 'Four (4) Entries maximum' on the $10,400; the Caesars 2026 flyer allows one first-break re-entry plus a $50 add-on; the Valuetown sheet prices later flights ('all subsequent buy in's after the initial buy in will be $200'). The Venetian's 37 audited structures print no entry rule in any form.
questions.missing: One sentence from each of the six Strip rooms saying whether additional entries are permitted or prohibited in this series, plus a named rule document for the 71 'no structure sheet linked' Venetian rows.
questions.how_to_close: One e-mail or phone call per room (The Venetian 702.414.7657, Wynn 702.770.7654, Bellagio 702.693.7291) asking: for event X on date Y, is a player limited to one entry, and are rebuys or add-ons offered? Quote the answer and its date on the row.

questions.question: When a room publishes both a summary article and a schedule document, do they agree on price?
questions.why_it_matters: A row read from the friendly page can be wrong in a way the schedule document would have caught. Buy-in drives the trip cost, the ranking ratio and whether an entry fits a budget.
questions.we_have: For Caesars Palace they do not, and the disagreement was found on 2026-11-17. The property's 2026 daily flyer prices 10 AM $100, 2 PM $160, 6 PM $100 and 9 PM $160, prints the fee split for each price, and allows one re-entry inside the first break; the property's own July 2026 article says “Every event carries a $100 buy-in”. The four rows now show the flyer price with the article sentence quoted beside them. Bellagio is a second instance of the same failure mode: its Saturday sheet titles the event $1,100 while rule 07 of the same sheet prices “the $600 Buy-in”, so that buy-in is left blank and flagged rather than guessed.

questions.how_to_close: Fetch each room's schedule document and its summary page in the same sync run and diff buy-in, guarantee, registration close and entry rules mechanically — both texts are already stored under data/raw/, so the comparison is arithmetic, not research. suggestions.title: Track each hotel's reservation-terms page as the fee source, not its marketing fee page
suggestions.problem: The figures the trip actually needs — mandatory resort fee, whether the fee is taxed, the per-occupant charge, the cancellation deadline — live on the property's Hotel Reservation Terms page, the document a guest agrees to. The pages called “resort fee” are marketing surfaces: Bellagio's 404s, Caesars' prints no amount, and one earlier pass carried a claim about ARIA publishing two fees on two official pages that could not be reproduced on any ARIA page.
suggestions.proposal: Standardise on <property>/en/terms-and-conditions.html (MGM) and the equivalent legal terms page elsewhere as the tracked source for fee, tax base, check-in/out, occupancy charge and cancellation, and read the operator's parking rate table for parking. That is how Bellagio and ARIA got filled in on 2026-11-17: $55.00 + tax, $50 + tax per extra occupant, 72-hour deadline, $20 self-park for registered guests, $40 valet.
suggestions.impact: medium-high — it turns blank hotel rows into comparable ones and removes the temptation to accept a third-party fee figure; the same page also settles whether the resort fee is taxed, which the true-cost formula depends on
suggestions.effort: low per property — one URL and the existing fact extractor
suggestions.decision_needed: Yes — approve extending the terms-page rule to Wynn/Encore, Caesars, Horseshoe, Harrah's and Treasure Island (Caesars-owned terms pages are worded per offer, so their deadline may only be readable inside a booking quote), and approve publishing the fee as a floor when no dated room rate exists.
suggestions.status: partly implemented — Bellagio and ARIA now read from their terms pages; the other properties still cite their fee pages

suggestions.title: Decide whether recurring evening slates count toward the trip total automatically
suggestions.problem: The day plan now lists each room's recurring events under the days their printed weekdays cover (111 of the placements in this window start at or after the lead event's registration deadline, so a second entry is arithmetically possible). But the trip calculator only counts events you tick, and the recurring rows are undated, so they cannot be scheduled into the total by date.
suggestions.proposal: Either (a) let the calculator accept “N evenings of this recurring slate” as a first-class line with the weekday constraint checked against the trip dates, or (b) leave it manual and print the weekday evidence on the row only. Option (a) makes the 8 AM–close day real; option (b) keeps every counted entry tied to one printed calendar row.
suggestions.impact: medium — it changes the trip cost materially (a Caesars evening adds $160 of entry and $50 of add-on per day) without any new data
suggestions.decision_needed: Yes — choose (a) or (b). Nothing was assumed here: the recurring rows stay unticked in the calculator and the plan lists them as options, not entries.

flags.detail: The PDF's title block says 'NLH $1100 BUY-IN', the Bellagio poker page lists 'SATURDAYS | $1,000 NLH', and rule 07 on the same sheet says 'Of the $600 Buy-in'. Its rule 04 also schedules the 'Combined Final Day 2 (9/13/26)'. The buy-in is therefore left blank, the row is not scheduled, and it needs a fresh sheet from the room before any money is committed.

flags.item: Wynn's daily slate is printed as a standing offer with no calendar dates, and the sheet itself says it may be suspended during other series
flags.detail: 'The Tournament will be offered Monday-Thursday and may be suspended during Seniors Events, Classic Events, or other Tournament Series.' Wynn runs its own WPT series from 2026-11-27 to 2026-12-21, so whether the $200/$240/$160 dailies run on any given trip date is not established by either document. Those rows carry no date and are never placed in the day plan.

flags.item: Caesars Palace's two official pages disagree on the daily buy-in: the explore page says every event carries $100, the 2026 daily flyer prints $160 at 2 PM and 9 PM
flags.detail: The Caesars explore page states four daily NLH tournaments at 10 a.m., 2 p.m., 6 p.m. and 9 p.m., 'every event carries a $100 buy-in', 20,000 chips, a $1,000 guarantee, 20-minute levels and a $50 add-on. The dedicated 2026 daily flyer PDF (re-checked live 2026-11-17 after the 2025 flyer was retired and 404ing) prints per-slot buy-ins — $100 at 10 a.m. and 6 p.m., $160 at 2 p.m. and 9 p.m. — plus the fee splits ($70/$30 and $115/$45), the add-on split ($45/$5), registration closing at the start of level 7, and rule 3: 'Participants may only register themselves, but may re-enter, by paying the entry fee, upon elimination within the first break of play.' The rows follow the dedicated, dated flyer (document of record for the schedule) and carry its excerpts; the explore page's blanket $100 sentence stays quoted on the row as the conflicting official statement. Single-entry status remains unverified on both sources — the printed re-entry rule is evidence of the opposite, so the rows stay in the spend-advantage section. Rows stay unranked because the slate prints no calendar dates.
flags.note: updated 2026-11-17 (session arena/3082d6d9-poker4): the retired 2025 flyer (HTTP 404) was replaced by the live 2026 flyer; per-slot buy-ins, fee splits, the re-entry rule and the explore-page conflict are now recorded on the rows. Earlier note: renumbered from F18 on merge with main, where that id was already used by another session.

flags.item: Wynn prints its late-registration deadlines as blind levels, not clock times, so a clock-based fallback cannot be computed for those rows
flags.detail: Most WPT sheets read 'available until the start of level 9' and only some add '(approximately 4:30 p.m.)'. The clock figure is missing on the majority of the 69 sheets. Consequence: the day plan can only offer a fallback where the printed deadline is a time, which is why 13 of the 38 planned days carry no defensible second entry.

flags.item: Primary Gaming Corridor membership (13.38% vs 13.00%) not checked property by property
flags.detail: The Clark County letter of 15 Nov 2016 sets 13.38% for properties inside the Primary Gaming Corridor, 13.00% for stadium-district properties outside it, and only the 0.5% LVCVA increase outside both. It refers to the PGC map on the county website but does not reproduce it. The Venetian's own terms print 13.38% (read live 2026-11-17). Wynn's rate is now sourced to the county letter and Treasure Island's to its offer-terms page, but neither property's map membership has been checked. Action: open the county PGC map and confirm each property before its rate is treated as confirmed. The letter is dated 15 Nov 2016. The current Clark County code (CCC 4.08) was not read in this session; the 13.38% figure is corroborated by the Venetian's live 2026 terms page, not by a current county document.

flags.item: data/room-facts.json carried sha256 values that did not match the raw captures it cites
flags.detail: Re-running tools/room_extract.py recomputed the hashes of data/raw/wynn-wpt-terms.txt and data/raw/wynn-daily-structures.txt. The committed values were stale. The regenerated file changes only those sha256 fields (commit 7c5767d). The raw captures were not changed. Re-committed 2026-11-18 (session e1004114, E2): tools/room_extract.py output is byte-stable across two runs and the recorded hashes now equal the sha256 of the committed captures (wynn-wpt-terms.txt 89689651…, wynn-daily-structures.txt 856079fd…, caesars-daily-flyer-2026.txt cdcb4178…).

flags.item: Daily poker4 monitor (tournament-monitor.yml) failed on its scheduled runs; cron removed 2026-11-18
flags.detail: The workflow "Daily schedule + source-change monitor" failed at its step "Verify the site before committing" on run 44190052816 (2026-11-17 22:26 UTC) and on three earlier push runs. The CI log could not be downloaded (EOF), so the exact failing check is unknown. On 2026-11-18 the same verify step (tools/verify_poker4.py) passes locally on the committed tree (20 pages, 94 tournament rows, 57 sources), and the same job rebuilds the legacy poker4/ sub-site, which is not the published root site. Decision (session e1004114, E3): the scheduled trigger was removed rather than repaired; manual dispatch remains. The published root site and its Pages deploy were not affected.

flags.item: Venetian DSE IV structure sheet 25 (satellites #45/#46/#48) prints an inconsistent blind line at level 25: big blind ante 120,000 with blinds 75,000-125,000
flags.detail: Live re-read of the official sheet (https://www.venetianlasvegas.com/content/dam/vlvweb/casino/poker/deepstack/2026/structures/dse_nov_2026-structure_25.pdf) on 2026-11-17 shows level 25 as '25 | 15 | 120,000 | 75,000-125,000'. Every surrounding level follows the 75k/150k-style progression (26 is 150,000 / 75,000-150,000), so the printed 125,000 big blind conflicts with the 120,000 ante on the same line. Published rows copy the sheet verbatim; no correction is inferred. The satellite structure past level 24 rarely matters (registration closes after level 6), but the sheet itself is internally inconsistent and is flagged for room confirmation.

flags.item: LINQ and Flamingo (added 2026-11-18): resort fee, room tax, parking and rate-specific cancellation are not confirmed on an official page
flags.detail: Both properties were added to the walking set because they sit on the Strip about 7 and 10 walking minutes from the Venetian poker room. The official caesars.com pages (fetched 2026-11-18) print the addresses (3535 and 3555 Las Vegas Blvd South) and a promotional banner 'Free cancellation up to 48 hours before check-in. Terms apply.' — that banner is not a rate-specific policy. No official resort-fee amount was found on either page. Third-party listings give Flamingo fees of $42, $50 and $56.63 and conflict with each other, so none is used. Fee, tax and parking cells stay blank until a Caesars page prints them.

flags.item: Walk re-capture tool named in the walk data does not exist in the repository
flags.detail: data/walk-measurements.json and data/walks.json both give 'Re-capture with: python3 tools/walk_capture.py'. No such file is in tools/ (checked 2026-11-18). The 2026-11-17 and 2026-11-18 walks were copied from Google Maps directions pages by hand. Only the date of each capture is recorded, not the time.

flags.item: Legacy data/hotels.json holds unmeasured walking estimates for LINQ and Flamingo that conflict with the measured walks; they are not used
flags.detail: data/hotels.json (the first-generation hotel file; the current build does not read it) gives estimated walks of 13 min for LINQ and 18 min for Flamingo, described in that file as estimates from straight-line geography and not verified. The measured Google Maps walks are 7 min (LINQ) and 10 min (Flamingo). The estimates are kept only as an archive. The estimated minutes do not appear on the published pages (checked 2026-11-18 by searching the built HTML for those values in the LINQ and Flamingo rows). Removing the file is a decision for the owner (see suggestions).

flags.item: structure-audit.json's Wynn daily summary omits the re-entry wording that the sheet prints
flags.detail: Read live 2026-11-18 from the Wynn daily structures PDF: the nightly $160 NLH $10,000 GTD sheet (6 PM, 'Nightly Monday-Sunday') prints 'The Tournament entry fee, as well as the re-entry fee, is $160' and 'Registration, re-entries, and one (1) add-on per entry will be available until the start of level 9 (approximately 9:00 p.m.)'. Another sheet earlier in the same PDF (title cut off at a capture boundary) prints the same re-entry clause. The Friday $240 sheet's re-entry clause ('Re-entry is NOT allowed') and the Monday–Thursday $200 sheet's wording were captured verbatim by the sync (data/room-facts.json) but were not re-read live in this session. The published rows WYNN-DAILY-1 to -4 (data/site-events.json) carry re-entry correctly (confirmed_allowed, or forbidden for the Friday sheet) and are excluded from the single-entry list. However data/structure-audit.json's W_DAILY record captures only the Friday 'Rebuy & Add on' line and the '$200 Entry Fee' guarantee text, so that summary is incomplete. Cite the room-facts rows, not the audit summary, for Wynn daily rules. The audit clause extractor should be re-run; not changed in this session.

flags.item: Venetian parking: two official parking rules apply to different guests; a trip budget must say which one applies
flags.detail: Read live 2026-11-18. The Venetian poker room page: 'Non-registered hotel guests who play for three hours or more in our tournaments or cash games receive complimentary self-parking.' The Venetian hotel terms page: 'The daily fee for registered hotel guests is $20/day, seven days a week. For non-hotel guests, the fee is $20, Monday – Thursday, and $25/day Friday – Sunday. Valet parking is $40/day.' and 'Venetian Rewards Sapphire members and above receive complimentary self-parking'. The poker-room comp is play-dependent (three hours of play) and is not a hotel rate; a hotel-guest trip cost should use the hotel-terms fee unless the player qualifies for the Sapphire comp. The hotel terms page is the source for the $20/day figure.
